JobPipe — full documentation
================================

What it is
----------
JobPipe is a free, no-signup, local-first job and freelance application
tracker. It runs entirely in the browser. There is no backend, no
account system, no paid plan, and no tracking. The source code is MIT
licensed at https://github.com/hamzabhulla/JobPipe and the author is
Hamza Bhulla (https://hamzabhulla.vercel.app).

Features
--------
- Kanban board with five stages: Saved, Applied, Interview, Offer,
  Rejected. Drag and drop between stages and within a stage, keyboard
  reordering, and a status menu on every card. On mobile, one column
  is shown at a time with swipe or buttons to switch columns.
- Job form: company, role, link, platform (LinkedIn, Upwork, Fiverr,
  Email, Other), type (full-time, contract, freelance), rate, location
  (remote, hybrid, onsite), applied date, follow-up date, notes, tags,
  and contact name.
- Proposal templates with placeholders {company}, {role}, {name}, and
  {skills}. Pick a template and a job, fill in name and skills, and
  copy the rendered text to the clipboard.
- Follow-up reminders: overdue and due-today sections at the top of
  the board, with snooze (+7 days) and done actions, plus an optional
  browser notification (at most once per day, only with permission).
- Search, filter by status, platform, and tag, and sort by newest,
  oldest, company, or follow-up date.
- Statistics: applications per week (last 8 weeks), response rate,
  and interview rate, plus counts by stage, drawn as lightweight SVG.
- JSON export and import: export downloads a versioned JSON file;
  import validates with zod and asks for confirmation before it
  replaces all current data.
- Dark and light themes (system default, saved in localStorage).
- Keyboard shortcuts: N for a new job, / to focus search, Esc to
  close dialogs, ? for the shortcuts help dialog.
- First-run empty state with a "Load sample data" option.
- Progressive web app: installable, works offline after first load.

Data model
----------
Job: id (UUID), company, role, link, platform, type, rate (free text,
for example "$50/hr"), location, status, appliedAt (YYYY-MM-DD or
null), followUpAt (YYYY-MM-DD or null), notes, tags (array of
strings), contactName, order (position within its status column),
createdAt and updatedAt (epoch milliseconds).
Template: id, title, body (raw text with placeholders), createdAt,
updatedAt.
Settings: a single row (id "settings") with theme, notifications
enabled, and whether sample data was loaded.
Storage: IndexedDB via Dexie.js, database name "jobpipe", with
versioned migrations (v1 initial schema, v2 date and tag indexes,
v3 updatedAt index). Order within a status column is always dense
0..n-1 and is maintained inside transactions on create, move, and
delete.

Privacy
-------
JobPipe has no server. Applications, templates, and settings are
stored only in the user's browser (IndexedDB). No analytics, no
tracking cookies, and no third-party trackers are used. Export
downloads a JSON file to the user's device; import reads a file the
user chose. Clearing browser site data deletes all JobPipe data, so
regular JSON exports are the backup mechanism.

FAQ
---
Is JobPipe really free? Yes. JobPipe is free and open source under
the MIT license. There is no paid plan, no premium tier, and no
feature locked behind payment.
Do I need to sign up to use JobPipe? No. JobPipe has no accounts and
no sign-up. Open the app and start tracking applications immediately.
Where is my data stored? Only in your browser, in IndexedDB on your
own device. JobPipe has no server and no database of its own, so your
applications are never sent to us or to anyone else.
Does JobPipe track me? No. JobPipe has no analytics, no tracking
cookies, and no third-party trackers. The only storage it uses is
your own browser storage for your applications, templates, and theme
preference.
Can I use JobPipe offline? Yes. JobPipe is a progressive web app.
After the first load, the app works offline because your data and the
app itself live in your browser.
What happens if I clear my browser data? Clearing browser data
deletes your JobPipe applications, because they live only in that
browser. Export a JSON backup regularly from inside the app, and
import it to restore your data.
Can I export my data? Yes. Export your applications and templates as
a JSON file at any time, and import a previously exported file back
into JobPipe. Import is validated and asks for confirmation before it
replaces your current data.

Install (local development)
---------------------------
Requirements: Node.js 20 or newer, npm, git.
  git clone https://github.com/hamzabhulla/JobPipe.git
  cd JobPipe
  npm install
  npm run dev
Then open http://localhost:5173/app/ (note the trailing slash in dev;
in production, /app works without it). Run tests with npm test,
typecheck with npm run typecheck, and build with npm run build
(output in dist/).

Limitations
-----------
- Data lives in one browser only; there is no sync between devices
  in this version. Optional cloud sync with a private key is on the
  roadmap, not yet released.
- Clearing browser data deletes all data; there is no server copy
  to restore from. JSON export is the backup.
- JobPipe does not find jobs, apply on your behalf, or integrate
  with job boards. It tracks applications you add yourself.
- Notifications require browser permission and only fire while the
  app is open or the browser can deliver them; the in-app follow-up
  panel is the reliable fallback.
- Rate is free text, not a number, so statistics never parse or
  convert rates.
